description: Kukulcan Space + Hiveflow: a Mexican team building an AI agent swarm that reads NASA's PSI microgravity combustion data (BASS, Saffire, FLEX, ACME, SAME), ranks and cross-checks the findings, and turns them into fire-safety insights for a 30% oxygen Moon Base, with a human expert approving every result. Looking for: Python/data science, combustion or physics, React/data viz, and storytelling/video. We speak Spanish & English.
summary:
Kukulcan Fire Lab is a web lab table for the people who design crewed spacecraft, stations, surface bases, pressurized rovers and suits. You pick the cabin atmosphere you are designing and the lab shows which of NASA's microgravity combustion tests sit near it, which investigations matter most, and what nobody has tested yet.

We harmonized the experimental tables of 19 combustion investigations from NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository, each with its own columns and units, into 1,946 records with common fields. That made one finding visible: 476 tests reach 30% oxygen or more, the atmosphere expected for a Moon base, and none of them burned a solid material. The highest oxygen level recorded for a solid sample is 22.2%.

The lab ranks investigations with the reasons shown, runs fire models and a cabin fire simulator, streams the test videos from NASA, and answers questions with citations through four MCP servers and a voice assistant that operates the whole table. It reports what was tested and says plainly when a design is extrapolation. It never certifies a material as safe.
details:
REPO:
https://github.com/johnolven/kukulcan-fire-lab

VIDEO

WHAT IT DOES

Kukulcan Fire Lab turns NASA's microgravity combustion archive into a design-stage evidence desk. The engineer sets a cabin (suit, capsule, transit spacecraft, station, surface base or rover) or any oxygen and pressure, and the lab answers three questions: what was tested near this design, which investigations matter most, and where the evidence stops.

HOW IT WORKS

- Harmonized dataset. The experimental tables of 19 investigations in NASA PSI use different columns and units (oxygen as fraction, percent or text; pressure in atm, mmHg or bar). We merged them into 1,946 records with common fields: fuel or material, oxygen, pressure, air flow, diluent, outcome, burn time. Values the source does not give stay blank and assumed values are marked.

- Verdict and ranking. For the current design the lab says, per fuel type, whether anything was tested nearby, and ranks all 24 combustion investigations out of 100 with the score broken down: fire-safety directness, proximity of tested conditions, material relevance, evidence volume, data availability.

- Evidence gaps. The headline: 476 tests reach 30% oxygen or more and none is a solid material. PSI also holds no partial-gravity data.

- Fire models and simulator. A cabin fire scenario simulator compares crew responses (ventilation off, masks, extinguisher, nitrogen flood, leaving the module), a live cabin emulation shows flame and smoke moving around a crew member, and five fire models run at the cabin's atmosphere. All are labeled as models with stated assumptions, separate from the test records.

- NASA footage and library. Test videos stream directly from NASA PSI and are matched to their test record. A library holds every resource listed by the challenge (Apollo 1, Apollo 13, the Mir fire, the Researcher's Guide, Spinoff articles) as citable passages, plus links to partner-agency work.

- Analytics on request. Describe a chart or table in plain language; a language model picks the fields and code computes every number from the records.

- Four MCP servers. Records, Resources, Voice and an Orchestrator that answers one question by calling the others and returns the trace of calls. Any MCP client can use them.

- Voice and chat. A voice assistant and a chat operate the whole table: they change views, move every control, run scenarios and quote the records.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

A fire-safety engineer no longer has to open 24 investigations with incompatible tables to learn whether a material or atmosphere has evidence behind it. Students get a guided way into the field. The harmonized dataset downloads as CSV for use in other models. The intended impact is earlier, better-informed decisions on cabin atmosphere and material selection for lunar and Martian habitats, and a clear list of the tests still missing.

TOOLS

Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, three.js, Python for data harmonization, the Model Context Protocol, the Anthropic API (Claude) for analyst text, orchestration and chart specifications, and Vapi for voice.

WHAT IS CREATIVE

The lab is organized around a design decision rather than a list of investigations. It treats missing evidence as a result, drawn on screen. One set of tools serves the dashboard, the voice, the chat and outside MCP clients.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

Honesty over polish. The lab never says a design is safe. It separates test records, models and history in its wording, marks extrapolation, cites the record or passage behind each statement, and labels every SI-generated text and the synthetic voice. Fire models are presented as calculations with assumptions, not as NASA results.
